Turkey In The Straw, X:4

This is Joe MacLean’s A major version of this old-time classic from his ‘Old Time Scottish Fiddle Music from Cape Breton Island’ recording. Written out here as a single reel, he plays it the way Old-Time or Bluegrass players would: AABB. I love cross-over tunes.

Here’s a variation for the first couple a phrases of the A part:

A3E CE E/E/E|FE E/E/E E2 AB|c3 {d}c2 cB|cB B/B/B BdcB|

↳ Posted by dancarney84 on August 1st, 2015.

Alternate Name

Re: Turkey In The Straw

Such a versatile tune. My teacher from Co. Mayo played it as a barndance.

Lots of American fiddlers play it as a breakdown in D which makes it to easy to play in both a higher and lower octave on the fiddle.

↳ Posted by FiddleJohn on June 15th, 2026.

Turkey In The Straw, X:7

The double stops can be quite tricky, but are very fun. This tune holds a special place in my heart as the first tune I learned.

↳ Posted by Jammin’Cellist on August 18th, 2026.

Re: Turkey In The Straw

My fiddler’s group sings to this one after playing it through. I know they’re incredibly nonsensical but they are a HIT a shows.
Our lyrics are:
A part:
Oh I had a litttle chickie but she wouldnt lay an egg,
So I poured hot water up and down her leg,
Oh the little chickie cried,
And the little chickie prayed,
And the little chickie layed me a hard-boiled-egg!
B part:
Hooray!
Fowl play!
Some yolk!
